# Results — Study 378 (ETF NAV Premium/Discount)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folk claim — *buy an ETF
trading **below its NAV** and you earn the discount back* — tested on three liquid
bond/EM/muni ETFs (**HYG, EMB, MUB**). True intraday iNAV / official NAV is not free on
yfinance, so we construct a transparent **NAV proxy**: a hedge-basket fair value per ETF
(a sister credit ETF + a rate leg), and define the transient **premium/discount basis** as
the ETF's detrended cumulative log-return residual to that proxy. A **discount** fires when
the basis z-score (rolling 252d) drops below **-1**; we enter the ETF 1 day later and
measure the **hedged harvest** — the residual earned back, net of the bond-market move.
Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — HYG, EMB, MUB + hedge legs (JNK, EMLC, LQD, TFI, IEF) (public, no key) |
| Window | 2012-01-03 → 2026-06-18 (**3,636** trading days; **~14.5** years) |
| NAV proxy | per-ETF hedge-basket fair value; basis = **detrended cumulative residual** — a **PROXY** for official NAV |
| Discount rule | basis z-score (rolling 252d) **< -1** (bottom of the prem/disc distribution) |
| Harvest / lag / costs | hedged residual over 5/10/20 days; **1-day entry lag**; one-way half-spread × (ETF + hedge) legs |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The official premium/discount is ETF close
> vs *published* NAV; we cannot see that on yfinance, so the basis here is the ETF's drift
> versus a **sister-ETF + rate hedge** — narrower than the true creation basket and
> **detrended** to be stationary. It tracks the *shape* of the real prem/disc (large,
> stress-driven, mean-reverting) but its level is a proxy, labelled throughout. The verdict
> does not hinge on the proxy's exact calibration: it hinges on the *magnitude vs cost* of
> the harvest, which a richer NAV series would only make smaller (the true creation/redeem
> arb is faster and tighter than our proxy).

## The signal — does the discount come back? (hedged harvest, pooled across ETFs)

The harvest is the **hedged residual return** over the hold (net of the bond market), so it
isolates "did the gap close?" from "did everything rally?". HAC = Newey-West t (overlapping
holds are autocorrelated). Pooled across all three ETFs:

| horizon | n discounts | mean discount depth | mean hedged harvest | win-rate | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 1,664 | — | **+0.0525%** | 56% | **+2.03** |
| 10-day | 1,663 | — | **+0.0496%** | 54% | **+1.24** |
| 20-day | 1,663 | — | **+0.0543%** | 53% | **+0.92** |

The discount **does** partially mean-revert — the pooled harvest is positive at every
horizon. But the magnitude is **~5 basis points**, the *t* only clears 2 at the shortest
5-day hold, and it **decays to t < 1 by 20 days**. A positive whisper, not a robust edge.

## It does not survive across the individual ETFs (10-day hold)

| ETF | n | mean discount depth | hedged harvest | win-rate | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **HYG** (US high yield) | 504 | −0.27% | **−0.0119%** | 45% | **−0.58** | 0.978 |
| **EMB** (EM sovereign $) | 597 | −1.47% | **+0.0696%** | 54% | +0.67 | 0.028 |
| **MUB** (US munis) | 562 | −0.36% | **+0.0835%** | 64% | **+2.40** | 0.000 |

The "edge" is **not a property of buying discounts** — it is one ETF (MUB) carrying the
pool. **HYG's discount earn-back is *negative*** (buying HYG cheap loses, hedged), and EMB
is a coin-flip. A signal that reverses sign across the very ETFs it's supposed to describe
is fragile by construction.

## Costs kill it — the gross harvest is smaller than the round-trip

A hedged discount trade round-trips the ETF **and** its hedge leg (buy+sell each). At a
realistic per-leg half-spread for these bond ETFs:

| half-spread per leg | round-trip cost (2 legs) | pooled gross (5-day) | **net** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 bp | 0.040% | +0.0525% | **+0.0125%** |
| **2 bp** | 0.080% | +0.0525% | **−0.0275%** |
| 3 bp | 0.120% | +0.0525% | **−0.0675%** |

At **2 bp per leg** — typical for HYG/EMB/MUB in calm markets — the strategy is already
**net negative**. The gross harvest (~5 bp) is *the same order of magnitude as one
half-spread*; there is no realistic cost at which buying the discount pays.

## Robustness — the *t* fades exactly as the discount gets "real"

| z threshold | n discounts | pooled gross (5-day) | win-rate | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| z < −0.5 | 3,047 | +0.0441% | 56% | **+2.83** |
| **z < −1.0** | 1,664 | +0.0525% | 56% | +2.03 |
| z < −1.5 | 846 | +0.0654% | 56% | **+1.53** |
| z < −2.0 | 403 | +0.1338% | 58% | +1.74 |

The *t* is largest at the *loosest* threshold (z < −0.5, where almost everything counts as a
"discount") and **fades as you tighten toward a genuine, deep discount**. That is the
opposite of a real structural edge, which should get *stronger* in the deep tail. The number
is a mild, broad mean-reversion, not a discount-harvesting machine.

## The discount widens exactly when you can't trade it

The deepest discounts are not spread through time — they **cluster in stress**:

| ETF | share of deepest-5% discount-days falling in 2020 | (uniform would be ~7%) | worst single discount |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| HYG | 24% | 7% | −1.04% (2016-05) |
| EMB | 22% | 7% | **−9.31% (2020-03-18)** |
| MUB | 25% | 7% | **−4.43% (2020-03-18)** |

About **a quarter** of every ETF's deepest discounts land in **2020** — a ~3× over-
concentration in the one window when the creation/redemption arbitrage that "closes the gap"
**broke**, dealer balance sheets froze, and the underlying bonds didn't trade. The biggest
"discounts" appear precisely when you can neither buy at NAV nor be sure the gap is a
mispricing rather than a stale-NAV artefact.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic AR(1) basis with a **planted per-day earn-back** injected only on
discount days, the detector + inference behave exactly as they must:

| planted edge | detected discounts | hedged harvest | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bp/day** (no edge) | 576 | −0.0642% | **−1.17** | 0.989 |
| **5 bp/day** (large edge) | 576 | +0.1702% | **+3.10** | 0.001 |

With **no** planted edge the test stays below 2 (no false positive, even with noise); a
large planted edge drives *t* to 3.1 and *p* to 0.001. The machinery is unbiased — so the
real-tape *t* of ~2 that **evaporates under costs, across ETFs, and as the discount
deepens** is exactly what a near-zero true edge looks like.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The discount *does* partially mean-revert: the pooled hedged harvest is
  positive (+5 bp/5-day, HAC *t* = 2.03). But it **fails t ≥ 2 at 10/20 days**, **reverses
  sign across ETFs** (HYG *t* = −0.58), and **weakens as the discount deepens** (t = 1.53 at
  z < −1.5). A mild, fragile mean-reversion — `WEAK`, not `REAL`, and the NAV input is an
  explicit **proxy**.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The gross harvest (~5 bp) is **smaller than one round-trip** on
  the ETF + hedge: net-negative at a routine 2 bp/leg half-spread. And the deepest discounts
  cluster in **March-2020-style stress**, when the arbitrage breaks and you cannot transact
  at NAV. There is no deployable edge.
- **"Free discount"? — BUSTED.** "Below NAV = on sale" is a structural illusion: the gap is
  mostly the *hedge basket* moving, what little reverts is bps, costs erase it, and the
  largest gaps appear exactly when they're least harvestable. The discount is real arithmetic
  about a fair-value proxy — it is not free money.
